Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> In April 2024, the canola market experienced significant price volatility, beginning with notable drops on April 11 and April 15. The period of fluctuation concluded with a strong rebound on April 22, which marked the largest single-day gain for the commodity since November 2023. <2> In its April 2024 Oil Crops Outlook, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) reported strong domestic demand for canola oil, largely driven by the biofuel industry. The report raised the forecast for U.S. canola oil use in biofuels to a record-high 4.0 billion pounds for the 2023-24 marketing year. [6, 9] To meet this demand, projections for the rapeseed crush in both the United States and Canada were increased to record highs. [9] Consequently, canola oil imports, primarily from Canada, were also forecast to be at a record level to satisfy the heightened U.S. demand. [9] <3> In January 2023, a record 376 million pounds of canola oil were used as feedstock for biofuel production in the United States, according to a U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Oil Crops Outlook report. This record consumption was driven by strong domestic demand, particularly for renewable diesel, which accounted for nearly 60% of the canola oil utilized in biofuels during that month. The surge in demand from renewable diesel facilities contributed to forecasts for record-high U.S. canola oil imports and overall use in biofuels for the 2023/24 marketing year. <4> In a report released on March 13, 2024, Statistics Canada provided crushing statistics for major oilseeds in both Canada and the United States for the 2023 calendar year. The report indicates that in the United States, oilseed processors crushed 2,058,625 tonnes of canola, which was a 19.2% increase from the total in 2022. Additionally, US processors crushed 61,267,971 tonnes of soybeans, a 2.6% increase from the previous year. The same report noted that Canadian processors crushed a record 10,522,947 tonnes of canola in 2023, a 20.0% increase from 2022. <5> Farm Credit Canada (FCC) released its 2024 Grains, oilseeds and pulses sector outlook, stating that falling commodity prices are expected to pressure margins. The report predicts that ample global soybean supplies for vegetable oil and biodiesel markets, along with a possible increase in U.S. soy acreage in 2024, will put pressure on both soybean and canola prices. <6> A weekly commodity report for the week ending September 22, 2023, indicated a significant drop in canola prices. [1] The price finished at $722, which was a 5.5% decrease from the previous week's price of $763.9. [1] Over the one-month period prior, prices had fallen by 9.3%. [1] <7> On August 29, 2023, Statistics Canada released its model-based estimates for principal field crops, forecasting a national canola production of 17.4 million tonnes. [1] This figure was derived from satellite imagery and agroclimatic data as of July 31, 2023. [4] The projected 7.1% decrease from the previous year was attributed to lower yields resulting from dry conditions across Western Canada. [1] Specifically, anticipated yields were expected to fall by 9.8% to 35.0 bushels per acre, which offset a 3.0% increase in harvested area. [1] This forecast was notably lower than many trade expectations. <8> By early June 2023, canola futures experienced a consistent and significant decline, causing the cash price expectation for the fall harvest to drop below $14 per bushel. This marked a substantial decrease from the approximately $19 per bushel price expectation at the beginning of the year. The roughly $5 per bushel drop represented an estimated decline in value of about $4.4 billion, assuming a 20 million tonne crop.

Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On June 13, 2025, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced its proposed Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) volume obligations for 2026 and 2027, which were higher than the market anticipated. [1, 2] This proposal for increased biofuel proportions in fuel led to a surge in canola futures prices, with a notable 10% rise in the hours following the announcement. The higher targets suggested a greater future demand for vegetable oils, such as canola, which are used as feedstocks for biodiesel. The proposed Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs) are expected to impact demand for both the current and upcoming crop seasons by necessitating an increase in U.S. biodiesel production. <2> Based on the USDA's Prospective Plantings report released on March 31, 2025, U.S. farmers intend to plant 2.56 million acres of canola in 2025, a 7% decrease from the record high of the previous year. Of this national total, North Dakota producers are expected to plant 2.05 million acres. This anticipated reduction in acreage was influenced by a drop in canola futures during March, which led some farmers in North Dakota to opt for planting different crops. <3> Based on the USDA's Prospective Plantings report, U.S. canola acreage for 2025 is forecast to decline by approximately 6-7% from the previous year to 2.56 million acres. [4, 5] Despite the projected decrease in planting, this would still represent the second-largest canola acreage on record. [5] The reduction is partly attributed to price shocks in March that influenced planting decisions, particularly in North Dakota, the largest canola-producing state. [1] In contrast to the reduced acreage, domestic canola crush demand is expected to be strong, with projections indicating a record high of 4.9 billion pounds, a 6% increase from the prior year. [3, 4] <4> A coalition of agricultural and biofuel organizations sent a letter to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator on March 17, 2025, urging the agency to establish timely and significant Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) volumes for 2026 and beyond. [2, 6, 7] The group, which includes the U.S. Canola Association, Clean Fuels Alliance America, the American Farm Bureau Federation, the American Soybean Association, the National Oilseed Processors Association, and the North American Renderers Association, specifically requested that the biomass-based diesel volume for 2026 be set at 5.25 billion gallons. [2, 5, 7] The letter argued that setting robust volumes would support American energy security, farm income, and continued investment in the clean fuels industry. [4] <5> China's State Council Tariff Commission announced on March 8, 2025, that it would impose a 100% tariff on Canadian canola oil and canola meal, with the tariffs officially taking effect on March 20, 2025. [2, 6] This measure was a response to Canadian tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles, steel, and aluminum. [3, 4, 6] The announcement caused a surge in canola futures on the Zhengzhou exchange in China. [5] The tariffs, which did not initially include raw canola seed, were seen as effectively closing the Chinese market to Canada's canola oil and meal industry. [2, 4] <6> The Northern Canola Growers Association (NCGA) and North Dakota State University (NDSU) Extension co-hosted the virtual 'Getting it Right in Canola Production' webinar on Friday, March 14, 2025. [1, 2, 4] The online event, held via Zoom from 8:30 a.m. to noon Central time, featured presentations from NDSU specialists on the latest research-based production information. [1, 4] Topics included agronomy recommendations, pest and disease management, and market forecasts, with a live Q&A session for participants. [4] The webinar was sponsored by the NCGA, and continuing education credits were available for certified crop advisers who attended the live event. [4] <7> In early February 2025, the Honey Bee Health Coalition reported that U.S. commercial beekeepers were discovering severe and sudden honey bee colony losses as they prepared for the California almond pollination season. Initial reports based on surveys from 234 beekeepers indicated average losses were well over 50%, with some operations experiencing up to 100% loss. The symptoms were described as being reminiscent of Colony Collapse Disorder (CCD). Later analysis confirmed these catastrophic losses, finding that commercial beekeepers lost an average of 62% of their colonies, which amounted to 1.6 million colonies, between June 2024 and March 2025. The coalition warned that these biological and economic hurdles could prevent beekeepers from rebuilding their operations for pollination and honey production in the coming year, potentially impacting the nation's produce supply. <8> On February 1, 2025, the Trump administration issued executive orders to impose tariffs on imports from Canada and Mexico, originally set to take effect on February 4, 2025. The administration has since postponed the implementation of these tariffs until March 4, 2025. The tariffs are set at a 25% rate on all goods from Mexico and most goods from Canada, with a lower 10% duty on Canadian energy and energy resources. This postponement is considered welcome news for the Canadian canola industry, as the United States is its largest export market. The Canola Council of Canada noted that the imposition of these tariffs would have a widespread and negative impact.

Prediction target period: from 2025-07-24 to 2025-08-08. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On June 13, 2025, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) announced its proposed Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) volume obligations for 2026 and 2027, which were higher than the market anticipated. [1, 2] This proposal for increased biofuel proportions in fuel led to a surge in canola futures prices, with a notable 10% rise in the hours following the announcement. The higher targets suggested a greater future demand for vegetable oils, such as canola, which are used as feedstocks for biodiesel. The proposed Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs) are expected to impact demand for both the current and upcoming crop seasons by necessitating an increase in U.S. biodiesel production. <2> Based on the USDA's Prospective Plantings report released on March 31, 2025, U.S. farmers intend to plant 2.56 million acres of canola in 2025, a 7% decrease from the record high of the previous year. Of this national total, North Dakota producers are expected to plant 2.05 million acres. This anticipated reduction in acreage was influenced by a drop in canola futures during March, which led some farmers in North Dakota to opt for planting different crops. <3> Based on the USDA's Prospective Plantings report, U.S. canola acreage for 2025 is forecast to decline by approximately 6-7% from the previous year to 2.56 million acres. [4, 5] Despite the projected decrease in planting, this would still represent the second-largest canola acreage on record. [5] The reduction is partly attributed to price shocks in March that influenced planting decisions, particularly in North Dakota, the largest canola-producing state. [1] In contrast to the reduced acreage, domestic canola crush demand is expected to be strong, with projections indicating a record high of 4.9 billion pounds, a 6% increase from the prior year. [3, 4] <4> A coalition of agricultural and biofuel organizations sent a letter to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator on March 17, 2025, urging the agency to establish timely and significant Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) volumes for 2026 and beyond. [2, 6, 7] The group, which includes the U.S. Canola Association, Clean Fuels Alliance America, the American Farm Bureau Federation, the American Soybean Association, the National Oilseed Processors Association, and the North American Renderers Association, specifically requested that the biomass-based diesel volume for 2026 be set at 5.25 billion gallons. [2, 5, 7] The letter argued that setting robust volumes would support American energy security, farm income, and continued investment in the clean fuels industry. [4] <5> China's State Council Tariff Commission announced on March 8, 2025, that it would impose a 100% tariff on Canadian canola oil and canola meal, with the tariffs officially taking effect on March 20, 2025. [2, 6] This measure was a response to Canadian tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles, steel, and aluminum. [3, 4, 6] The announcement caused a surge in canola futures on the Zhengzhou exchange in China. [5] The tariffs, which did not initially include raw canola seed, were seen as effectively closing the Chinese market to Canada's canola oil and meal industry. [2, 4] <6> The Northern Canola Growers Association (NCGA) and North Dakota State University (NDSU) Extension co-hosted the virtual 'Getting it Right in Canola Production' webinar on Friday, March 14, 2025. [1, 2, 4] The online event, held via Zoom from 8:30 a.m. to noon Central time, featured presentations from NDSU specialists on the latest research-based production information. [1, 4] Topics included agronomy recommendations, pest and disease management, and market forecasts, with a live Q&A session for participants. [4] The webinar was sponsored by the NCGA, and continuing education credits were available for certified crop advisers who attended the live event. [4] <7> In early February 2025, the Honey Bee Health Coalition reported that U.S. commercial beekeepers were discovering severe and sudden honey bee colony losses as they prepared for the California almond pollination season. Initial reports based on surveys from 234 beekeepers indicated average losses were well over 50%, with some operations experiencing up to 100% loss. The symptoms were described as being reminiscent of Colony Collapse Disorder (CCD). Later analysis confirmed these catastrophic losses, finding that commercial beekeepers lost an average of 62% of their colonies, which amounted to 1.6 million colonies, between June 2024 and March 2025. The coalition warned that these biological and economic hurdles could prevent beekeepers from rebuilding their operations for pollination and honey production in the coming year, potentially impacting the nation's produce supply. <8> On February 1, 2025, the Trump administration issued executive orders to impose tariffs on imports from Canada and Mexico, originally set to take effect on February 4, 2025. The administration has since postponed the implementation of these tariffs until March 4, 2025. The tariffs are set at a 25% rate on all goods from Mexico and most goods from Canada, with a lower 10% duty on Canadian energy and energy resources. This postponement is considered welcome news for the Canadian canola industry, as the United States is its largest export market. The Canola Council of Canada noted that the imposition of these tariffs would have a widespread and negative impact.
